links.outcome: Diagnostic and therapeutic F1 and RAGAS with vs without guideline retrieval grounding
links.effect: RAG generally improved diagnostic and therapeutic accuracy, magnitude varied by model; SLMs benefited most consistently; Mixtral with RAG had top F1 (72% Dx, 73% Tx) and RAGAS 81%.
links.quote: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) generally improved diagnostic and therapeutic accuracy, although the magnitude of improvement varied considerably depending on model architecture ( Table 1 ).

links.outcome: Proportion of responses unsuitable for clinical use due to unsafe or hallucinated recommendations
links.effect: Expert review found 9% of generated responses not suitable for clinical use, including hallucinated therapeutic recommendations based on assumed prior treatments.
links.quote: However, expert review by the rheumatologists showed that 9% of generated responses were not suitable for clinical use.

links.outcome: LLMs generating treatment recommendations with unsafe content
links.effect: 9% of responses were unsuitable for clinical use, partly from unsafe or hallucinated therapeutic recommendations; authors state no model should be used without expert supervision.
links.quote: As a result, none of the evaluated models should be used without expert supervision.
